sections.normalized_html:
We are given the equation [MATH: \dfrac{1}{9n} = \dfrac{2f}{t}] and asked to solve for [MATH: f] in terms of [MATH: t] and [MATH: n.]

To eliminate the denominators, we use cross multiplication: [MATH: 1 ⋅ t|= 2f ⋅ 9n; t|= 18fn]

Now divide both sides by [MATH: 18n] to isolate [MATH: f{:}] [MATH: (t)/(18n)|= (18fn)/(18n); (t)/(18n)|= f]

Rewriting with [MATH: f] on the left-hand side, we get the correct answer: [MATH: f = \dfrac{t}{18n}]

We are given the equation [MATH: g = -12 + \dfrac{48}{w}] and asked to solve for [MATH: w] in terms of [MATH: g.]

First, we add [MATH: 12] to both sides: [MATH: g + 12|= − 12 + (48)/(w) + 12; g + 12|= (48)/(w)]

Now we multiply both sides of the equation by [MATH: w]: [MATH: (g + 12) ⋅ w|= (48)/(w) ⋅ w; w(g + 12)|= 48]

Finally, we divide both sides by [MATH: g + 12] to isolate [MATH: w{:}] [MATH: (w(g + 12))/(g + 12)|= (48)/(g + 12); w|= (48)/(g + 12)]

Therefore, the correct answer is [MATH: w = \dfrac{48}{g + 12}.]

sections.normalized_html:
The variables [MATH: p] and [MATH: q] are related by the equation
[MATH: p = \dfrac{7q - 4}{q}.] Express [MATH: q] in terms of [MATH: p.]
sections.readable_text:
The variables [MATH: p] and [MATH: q] are related by the equation
[MATH: p = \dfrac{7q - 4}{q}.]
Express [MATH: q] in terms of [MATH: p.]

sections.normalized_html:
Multiplying both sides of the given equation by [MATH: q] gives [MATH: pq = 7q - 4.] Subtracting [MATH: 7q] from both sides, we get [MATH: pq - 7q = -4.] Factoring out [MATH: q] on the left-hand side, we get [MATH: q(p - 7) = -4.] Finally, dividing both sides by [MATH: p - 7] yields [MATH: q = \dfrac{-4}{p - 7}.]

So, the correct answer is [MATH: q = \dfrac{-4}{p - 7}.]

Question (MC, H)

Stem:
Explanation:

We are given the equation [MATH: \dfrac{24}{x} = \dfrac{24}{y} + \dfrac{24}{z} - \dfrac{24}{w}.]

First, we factor out the common factor of [MATH: 24] on the right-hand side: [MATH: \dfrac{24}{x} = 24\left(\dfrac{1}{y} + \dfrac{1}{z} - \dfrac{1}{w}\right)]

Then, we divide both sides by [MATH: 24]: [MATH: \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{1}{y} + \dfrac{1}{z} - \dfrac{1}{w}]

To isolate [MATH: \dfrac{1}{y},] we subtract [MATH: \dfrac{1}{z}] and add [MATH: \dfrac{1}{w}] from both sides: [MATH: \dfrac{1}{y} = \dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{w}]

We now combine the terms on the right-hand side using a common denominator of [MATH: xzw]: [MATH: (1)/(y)|= (1)/(x) − (1)/(z) + (1)/(w); = (zw)/(zw) ⋅ (1)/(x) − (xw)/(xw) ⋅ (1)/(z) + (xz)/(xz) ⋅ (1)/(w); = (zw − xw + xz)/(xzw).]

Taking the reciprocal of both sides gives the desired relation: [MATH: y = \dfrac{xzw}{zw - xw + xz}]
